title: JWT IN 60 SECONDS
summaryPoints: A JWT is a header, a payload and a signature joined by dots.
The header and payload are Base64URL text, not encrypted, so anyone can decode them.
The signature is made with a secret key and proves the token was not changed.
Changing the payload breaks the signature, so the server rejects the token.
Signed is not secret: never put passwords or private data in a JWT.

chapters.name: HOOK
chapters.summary: Every login ends in a string called a JWT.

chapters.name: PARTS
chapters.summary: A JWT is three parts joined by two dots.

chapters.name: READABLE
chapters.summary: The header and payload are only Base64, so anyone can read them.

chapters.name: SIGNATURE
chapters.summary: The signature is a seal made with a secret key only the server knows.

chapters.name: TAMPER
chapters.summary: Change one letter of the payload and the seal no longer matches.

chapters.name: TAKEAWAY
chapters.summary: Signed does not mean secret: never put secrets in a JWT.
